method: Targeted primary publication/official statement full-text audit; not a systematic review, formal GRADE assessment, human validation or empirical product validation.

sources.title: American College of Sports Medicine Position Stand. Resistance Training Prescription for Muscle Function, Hypertrophy, and Physical Performance in Healthy Adults: An Overview of Reviews
sources.population_design_dose: 137 reviews; randomized healthy-adult interventions of at least six weeks, mainly inexperienced participants.
sources.findings: Many resistance configurations improve outcomes; individualize to goals and participation. Overload supports continued development; failure is unnecessary. Exact RIR targets remain uncertain.
sources.locator: Europe PMC PMC12965823 fullTextXML: Methods/Eligibility, Tables 3–4, Discussion; PubMed identity verified.
limitations: Group-level synthesis; protocol overlap; limited advanced-athlete evidence; exact program superiority cannot be inferred.
counterevidence: The 2026 discussion questions rigid conformity to the 2009 prescription details.

sources.title: Compatibility of Concurrent Aerobic and Strength Training for Skeletal Muscle Size and Function: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sources.population_design_dose: 43 studies; healthy adults; supervised concurrent versus identical strength-only training for at least four weeks.
sources.findings: Average maximal-strength and whole-muscle hypertrophy effects were compatible; explosive outcomes were less favorable, especially same-session training.
sources.locator: PMC8891239: Methods, Results, Discussion; same-session versus separated subgroup.
limitations: Mostly moderate-quality small studies; broad training-status groups; sparse dose/intensity reporting; subgroup spacing is not a universal minimum.
counterevidence: Endpoint-specific fiber findings differ in R4-S03; no blanket absence-of-interference claim.

sources.title: The Effects of Concurrent Aerobic and Strength Training on Muscle Fiber Hypertrophy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sources.population_design_dose: 15 studies; healthy adults; at least four weeks; fiber rather than whole-muscle outcomes.
sources.findings: Possible small fiber-hypertrophy attenuation; running subgroup findings were based on few studies.
sources.locator: Europe PMC PMC9474354 fullTextXML: Abstract and Discussion, including measurement limitations.
limitations: Small studies, biopsy variability, mostly moderate quality; running subgroup only three studies.
counterevidence: Whole-muscle findings in R4-S02 are more favorable; endpoints must remain distinct.

sources.title: Effects of Different Training Intensity Distribution in Recreational Runners
sources.population_design_dose: 38 recreational runners; eight-week polarized versus focused moderate-intensity programs; no strength training.
sources.findings: Both programs improved several running outcomes without a demonstrated between-group advantage; multiple intensity structures can be defensible.
sources.locator: Publisher full text: Materials and Methods, training Table 2, Results, Discussion.
limitations: Small study; volume differed; calibrated laboratory intensities; not a hybrid trial or proof of an exact cruise recipe.
counterevidence: Against a universal optimal intensity distribution or transfer of field pace to physiological threshold.

sources.title: A Systematic Review Examining the Approaches Used to Estimate Interindividual Differences in Trainability and Classify Individual Responses to Exercise Training
sources.authors: Bonafiglia JT, Preobrazenski N, Gurd BJ
sources.population_design_dose: 149 studies across exercise types; audit of individual-response methods.
sources.findings: Observed variation mixes measurement noise, within-person variation and possible training response. Inadequate response thresholds inflate classifications.
sources.locator: PMC8606564: Abstract, Methods, Results and Discussion.
limitations: Few included studies estimated true individual differences; no validated count threshold for a product learning model.
counterevidence: Observed better scheduling response cannot establish causal physiology or immutable responder traits.

sources.title: Monitoring the athlete training response: subjective self-reported measures trump commonly used objective measures: a systematic review
sources.authors: Saw AE, Main LC, Gastin PB
sources.population_design_dose: Athletes in training; repeated validated well-being questionnaires and concurrent objective measures.
sources.findings: Subjective well-being can inform acute/chronic monitoring; complementary observations and individual baselines matter.
sources.locator: Europe PMC PMC4789708 fullTextXML: Discussion including implementation and limitations; PubMed identity verified.
limitations: Heterogeneous methods, recall intervals, small studies, nontraining stress and selective reporting; RPE excluded as a different construct.
counterevidence: No validated fatigue diagnosis or universal readiness cutoff; a single bad signal need not justify change.

sources.title: Effects of tapering on performance in endurance athletes: A systematic review and meta-analysis
sources.authors: Wang Z, Wang YT, Gao W, Zhong Y
sources.population_design_dose: 14 studies of endurance tapering; heterogeneous events and designs.
sources.findings: Reduced training volume with retained intensity/frequency can improve time-trial performance; pooled taper configurations are context dependent.
sources.locator: PLOS full text: Methods, Results/subgroups, Discussion and limitations.
limitations: Not a direct joint running-plus-strength race-week recipe; subgroup findings do not establish individual optimal reductions.
counterevidence: Does not authorize deleting strength, adding pre-taper overload, or a universal hybrid taper.

sources.title: The GRONORUN study: is a graded training program for novice runners effective in preventing running related injuries? Design of a Randomized Controlled Trial
sources.population_design_dose: Protocol: eligible healthy adults 18–65 with no regular running in prior year and no recent lower-limb injury.
sources.findings: Documents feasible run/walk entry with comfortable speech and walking preparation; protocol alone establishes no injury benefit.
sources.locator: Europe PMC PMC1821023 fullTextXML: Eligibility and Training program.
limitations: Design paper only; used as structural precedent, not efficacy evidence or universal novice dose.
counterevidence: Completed trial R4-S09 did not confirm the ten-percent prevention hypothesis.

sources.title: No effect of a graded training program on the number of running-related injuries in novice runners: a randomized controlled trial
sources.population_design_dose: 532 novice runners randomized to 13-week graded versus eight-week standard preparation.
sources.findings: No detected injury-rate advantage of the graded ten-percent program.
sources.locator: PubMed structured abstract; publisher PDF attempts failed; not sole prescriptive support.
limitations: ABSTRACT_ONLY in this session; no equivalence or proof of zero risk.
counterevidence: Challenges universal ten-percent safety claims; cannot specify individual safe progression.
